items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The CTE names `ws` and `agg` don't say what they hold, and the count column is a single letter, `c`. The outer alias is `a`. The `MAX(CASE WHEN ws.rn = 1 THEN ...)` pivot is a non-obvious trick. Layout and indentation are otherwise clean.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The structure is compact: two CTEs plus a final select. But the full `ORDER BY total_senses DESC, total_synsets DESC, distinct_domains DESC, wordid ASC` is written twice (inside `agg` and in the outer query). Changing the order means editing both copies.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: `LIMIT 500` runs inside `agg` before the inner `JOIN words`. If a wordid has no row in `words`, the result can have fewer than 500 rows. `rn` is computed before the `JOIN synsets`, so a missing synset could make `top_synsetid` NULL. The thresholds 2 and 500 come from the spec.

items.name: Semantically equivalent, not just equal on this data
items.name_zh: 语义等价而非仅在当前数据上相等
items.evidence: It keeps the HAVING thresholds, `COUNT(DISTINCT)` NULL behaviour, the top-synset tie-break (COUNT DESC, synsetid ASC) and the final ordering. But it relies on every `senses.wordid` existing in `words` (LIMIT before join) and every synsetid existing in `synsets` (rn before join), and the schema has no constraints guaranteeing either.
